issue: The ④ OUTCOME box headline reads 'CLEARS CAPACITY GATE (a)·(b)', which presents candidates (a) and (b) as having passed the capacity/throughput gate. This contradicts the figure's own caption ('three conditional candidates, each with its own open validation gate (not a settled verdict) ... no candidate is deployment-validated') and Table 12-1 on PDF 222 / printed 202, where row (b) verdict is 'conditional finalist — ✗ throughput at a single prefill host (~19.8K ≪ ~92K); prefill pool must itself scale to ~5 hosts'. The sub-line 'each needs ~5 hosts of prefill capacity' is a *condition* for clearing the gate, not a clearance, so the present-tense verb 'CLEARS' overstates the evidence.
evidence: Figure box text: 'CLEARS CAPACITY GATE (a)·(b) / each needs ~5 hosts of prefill capacity'. Caption: 'no candidate is deployment-validated; each must measure its gate (throughput for a/b, quality for c) at the target load'. Table 12-1 row (b) verdict column: 'conditional finalist — ✗ throughput at a single prefill host (~19.8K ≪ ~92K); prefill pool must itself scale to ~5 hosts (92K ÷ 19.8K ≈ 4.65)'.
acceptance_test: Reword the OUTCOME box so the figure matches the caption's 'open validation gate' and the table's 'conditional finalist', e.g. 'CONDITIONAL on capacity gate (a)·(b) — each needs ~5 prefill hosts (to be measured at target load)'. After the edit, a reader who looks only at the figure (not the caption) must not be able to conclude that (a) or (b) is deployment-validated to meet the SLO.

issue: Color mismatch between caption and drawing. The caption names the de-escalation direction 'green' in two places, but the figure draws the de-escalation arrow and its label in blue. Green is already used in the figure for the four tier boxes and the '▼ constraints → STOP' markers, so the caption's 'green' is wrong on two counts (it does not match the drawn color, and it collides with the color that denotes tiers/STOP).
evidence: Caption body: 'de-escalation (green) fires on privacy, data sovereignty, and cost'. Caption italic summary: 'de-escalation (green: privacy, data sovereignty, cost)'. Figure: right-side vertical dashed arrow and label 'DE-ESCALATE: privacy · sovereignty · cost' are rendered in blue; the tier boxes and '▼ constraints → STOP' text are rendered in green.
acceptance_test: Change the caption's 'de-escalation (green)' to 'de-escalation (blue)' in both the body sentence and the italic summary line (or, if the arrow is recolored green, reassign the tier/STOP color so green no longer denotes both). After the fix, the color word in the caption must equal the color of the drawn de-escalation arrow, and no single color may denote two different semantic roles.

figure: Figure 15.2, panel (b) (Decode bottleneck unaffected by caching)
issue: The red in-plot annotation ('diminishing gains / past ~b16 (no hard / plateau: goodput / still rises; tail / latency keeps rising)') is a dense 6-line block set in the smallest type in the figure; at the 150 dpi render its cap height is visibly smaller than the axis tick labels and appears to fall below the 8 pt print floor for figure in-text annotations.
evidence: Visual comparison on the rendered page: the red annotation glyphs are smaller than the '0/20/40/60/80/100' y-axis numerals and the '1/10' x-axis numerals, which are at or above the floor; the annotation is the only multi-line in-plot text and the tightest set.
acceptance_test: Enlarge the annotation to ≥8 pt, or reduce it to a short in-plot label (e.g. 'knee ~b16') and move the 'no hard plateau / tail latency keeps rising' clarification into the caption. Re-render and confirm the in-plot text meets the 8 pt floor.

issue: The x-axis quantity 'Avg prefix reuse' is used as the independent variable of the left plot but is never defined in the caption or the surrounding prose. A reader cannot tell whether it means the mean number of requests sharing a given prefix, the mean fraction of prompt tokens served from cache, or the mean reuse count per cached token — yet the curve's shape (100% at x=1, falling to ~60% at the right) depends on that definition.
evidence: Axis label: 'Avg prefix reuse'. Caption: 'prefill work vs average prefix reuse, as a percent of no-cache prefill work' — no operational definition given. Prose below the figure ('Goodput vs. Batch Size: the Cache Lever') also does not define it.
acceptance_test: Add a one-line definition to the caption, e.g. 'average prefix reuse = mean number of times a cached prefix block is reused across the request population (1 = no sharing, hence no prefill reduction)'. After the edit, the x=1 → 100% starting point must be self-evident from the definition.

issue: Wording tension between caption and in-plot annotation. The caption describes the right curve as 'rising until HBM bandwidth saturates', which a careful reader parses as an eventual flat plateau, while the in-plot annotation explicitly states 'no hard plateau: goodput still rises'. The intended meaning (asymptotic approach to the bandwidth ceiling, not a flat line in the shown range) is not stated in the caption.
evidence: Caption: 'batching raises decode goodput (right: decode goodput vs batch size, arbitrary goodput units, rising until HBM bandwidth saturates)'. In-plot red annotation: 'no hard plateau: goodput still rises; tail latency keeps rising'.
acceptance_test: Align the caption with the figure, e.g. 'rising, bending as it approaches the HBM-bandwidth ceiling (no hard plateau in the shown range)'. After the edit, the caption and the in-plot annotation must not be readable as 'eventually flat' vs 'never flat'.
